prerequisites: It is especially recommended to have passed the subject of Electrical Technology.
It is recommended to have completed the subjects corresponding to the basic training modules and those corresponding to the second year of the common module for the Industrial branch.

learning_outcomes.text: That the student is capable of integrating existing regulations and standards, permanent load conditions, and electrical energy supply conditions into the design criteria of a low-voltage electrical installation.
That the student is capable of distinguishing the technical and constructive characteristics of an electrical cable.
That the student is capable of identifying the operating principle and technical characteristics of the main elements that constitute the protection and switching equipment of an installation.
That the student is capable of using technical criteria for selecting cabling as well as protection and switching equipment during the design of an installation.
That the student is capable of understanding the operation and identifying the technical characteristics of transformers and induction electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: Switching and protection equipment. Electrical measurements. Tariffication.
Design and calculation of low-voltage electrical installations (BT).
Principles of operation of electrical machines.
Analysis of electrical safety conditions in an installation
Monitoring of a three-phase induction motor

assessment_methods.method: Practical Work (dimensioning of a low-voltage electrical installation)

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation in January, the final exam (EXF) counts for 80% of the final grade, requiring more than 3 points out of 10 in each thematic block and an average of 5 points out of 10 overall. A partial exam can liberate students from the first block of the final exam if passed with 5 or more. A practical work (TRB) accounts for 10% of the final grade, and laboratory activities (LAB) account for 10% (6% for practice guides and 4% for a final lab test), with LAB requiring a score above 5 to pass. The final grade is 0.8*EXF + 0.1*TRB + 0.1*LAB if EXF >= 5 and LAB >= 5, otherwise, the student fails. For June and July convocations, the final exam (EXF) is 90% and laboratory practices are 10%, both must be >= 5 to pass.
